hints: A critical city is one whose removal blocks every route from 1 to n.
In a directed graph, ordinary articulation points do not capture direction.
Find the dominator tree rooted at city 1.
analogy: A dominator is a checkpoint that every valid itinerary to a destination must pass.
example: With routes 1-2-3-5 and 1-2-4-5, the unavoidable cities are 1, 2 and 5.
algorithm: Run a directed dominator algorithm such as Lengauer-Tarjan from vertex 1. DFS-number reachable vertices, compute semidominators using reverse edges and union-find ancestor evaluation, then resolve each immediate dominator. Build the dominator tree and walk from n through immediate dominators to 1. Sort these vertices and print them.
correctness: A vertex dominates n precisely when every directed path from 1 to n includes it. The dominator tree represents the dominance relation by ancestry, so exactly the ancestors of n, including n and 1, are critical.
complexity: For n cities and m flights, Lengauer-Tarjan takes near-linear O((n+m) log n) time with a simple union-find implementation and O(n+m) space.
